findings.title: Used recovery code never marked as used for federated credentials
findings.body: For user-storage users, the credential stored is just a JSON list of raw codes. Validation in the real federated provider path never marks a code as used. In RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator, `allCodesUsed()` and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode()` operate on a model that the storage never updates. As a result, the same code can be reused indefinitely and the prompted code number never advances. The `removeStoredCredentialById` call is also applied to a federated credential ID, which will not work.

findings.title: Raw recovery codes sent to user storage in plaintext
findings.body: For federated storage the raw generated codes are serialized as JSON and passed as the challenge response. Local storage keeps only hashes. The codes are therefore stored unhashed in the external storage, a security downgrade. Metadata such as the user label and creation time are also lost.

findings.title: Unchecked Optional.get() calls
findings.body: `credentialModelOpt.get()` and `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` throw NoSuchElementException if no credential is found. This is more likely now that lookup spans two sources. Previously the same risk existed, but a clearer error should be produced.

findings.title: getCredentials NPE when user missing, and the credential type is not converted
findings.body: `getMyUser(user)` can return null, for example after the user is removed, and `myUser.recoveryCodes` then throws an NPE. Also, the recovery model is built via createFromValues, which re-hashes the codes. Because of that, the model's credential data differs from what isValid compares against, and the user label is never persisted.
